tool.help:
**What it does**
Hash BAM, CRAM and FASTQ files to verify data integrity.
For each pair of reads in a BAM/CRAM or FASTQ file a hash value is computed, composed of the readname, whether it is first or last in pair, sequence and quality value. All the hash values are summed up so the result is independent of the ordering within the files. The result can be compared to verify that a pair of FASTQ files contains the same read information as the aligned BAM/CRAM file.
-----
**BAM / CRAM**
Processes a number of BAM or CRAM files. Files are assumed to contain paired end reads. If you run with `--no-paired` all reads are treated as single end and a warning is displayed if any read is marked as "second in pair" in the file.
Each read must carry an `RG` (read group) tag; the checksum is reported per read group as `readgroup`, `checksum` and `readcount` (tab separated), one line per read group found in the file header.
For CRAM files that do not store the reference in their header, supply the reference FASTA file so the reads can be decoded.
-----
**FASTA**
Processes a number of FASTA files. All FASTA files are assumed to be single end reads with no quality information. To compare to a BAM file, run BamHash on the BAM with `--no-paired --no-quality`.
-----
**FASTQ**
Processes a number of FASTQ files. FASTQ files are assumed to contain paired end reads, such that the first two files contain the first pair of reads, etc. If any of the read names in a pair don't match, the program exits with failure.
-----
BamHash is Free and Open Source Software, see the [BamHash GitHub repository](https://github.com/DecodeGenetics/BamHash).
